content.text: The Firebase dependency graph is wired through Swift Package Manager, while MediaPipe remains CocoaPods. The runtime switch is intentionally DEBUG-gated and local by default, but the real risk now is whether Firestore DTO reads/writes, observers, and account deletion/export paths fail gracefully when remote data is missing, stale, or partially denied.

messages.text: I found one high-confidence Firebase compliance bug: the deletion flow currently attempts Firebase Auth deletion before the bounded Firestore cleanup. With owner-only Firestore rules, deleting the Auth user first can drop `request.auth` and make the client-allowed cleanup fail. I’m going to patch that order and add/adjust tests around the sequence.

content.text: I found one high-confidence Firebase compliance bug: the deletion flow currently attempts Firebase Auth deletion before the bounded Firestore cleanup. With owner-only Firestore rules, deleting the Auth user first can drop `request.auth` and make the client-allowed cleanup fail. I’m going to patch that order and add/adjust tests around the sequence.

messages.text: A second crash-prevention edge is in Firestore query limits. Several repo methods pass `0` after clamping negative limits; Firebase’s query `limit(to:)` is not a place I want to trust with zero or negative values. I’m going to make the Firestore database adapter return an empty snapshot/stream for non-positive limits before it touches the SDK.
